interventions.body:
WHAT I FOUND
**radiology_report**: The mpMRI prostate showed a focal, ill-defined hypointense lesion in the right peripheral zone, approximately 14 mm in greatest dimension, with corresponding restricted diffusion. Dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences showed early, intense enhancement. Impression was PI-RADS v2.1 score 4, Clinical T stage cT1c, and csPCa predicted probability 0.86231947.
**pathology_report**: Histological evaluation of the prostate tissue specimens revealed adenocarcinoma with a Gleason score of 3+4, corresponding to ISUP grade group 2. The tumour was located in the right peripheral zone and demonstrated a cribriform and glomeruloid growth pattern. A cribriform pattern was present. No perineural invasion was noted. The AI-predicted ISUP grade group (digital pathology) was grade group 4.
**previous_notes**: The patient presented for follow-up of known prostate cancer. PSA was 4.3 ng/mL, representing a significant rise from previous stable values. A repeat biopsy was decided upon to assess for histological progression.
**family_history**: Not recorded.
**psa_trend**: The PSA trajectory shows values of 1.1 (Jun 2022), 1.8 (Feb 2023), 1.1 (Oct 2023), 4.3 (Jun 2024), and 9.0 (Feb 2025).
**laboratory_results**: The most recent PSA was 9.0 ng/mL on 16 Jan 2025. Free PSA was 2.32 ng/mL (26% Free PSA). Other labs (Haemoglobin, WBC, Platelets, Creatinine, eGFR, Testosterone, Alkaline phosphatase, LDH) were within normal limits or not flagged.

WHAT IS NOT RECORDED
The specific findings regarding lymphovascular invasion (LVI), EPE, and ejaculatory duct/seminal vesicle involvement from the pathology report were not recorded. The patient's family history regarding prostate cancer was not recorded.

WHAT THIS SUPPORTS
The patient is a 68-year-old male with a PSA trajectory showing a significant rise to 9.0 ng/mL. The MRI confirmed a PI-RADS 4 lesion with a clinical T stage cT1c. The pathology confirms ISUP grade group 2 disease (Gleason 3+4) with high-risk architectural features. The missing LVI/EPE data is critical for the next management step.
